chunks: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Zayd al-Narsī, from ʿAlī ibn Mazyad, the companion of al-Sābirī, who said:

A man entrusted me with his estate and instructed me to perform hajj on his behalf. I examined it and found it to be a small amount that was not sufficient for hajj, so I asked Abū Ḥanīfah and the fuqahāʾ of Kūfah, and they said: Give it as charity on his behalf.

Then when I met ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥasan during tawaf, I asked him and said: A man from your followers from the people of Kūfah died and entrusted his estate to me, instructing me to perform hajj on his behalf. I examined it and it was not enough for hajj, so I asked the jurists among us, and they said: Give it as charity on his behalf. So I gave it as charity. What do you say? He said to me: Here is Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad in the Hijr, so go to him and ask him. I entered the Hijr, and there was Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام beneath the Mīzāb, facing the House and making du'a. Then he turned and saw me and said: What is your need? I said: A man died and entrusted his estate to me so that I should perform hajj on his behalf. I examined it and it was not enough for hajj, so I asked the jurists among us, and they said: Give it as charity.

He said: What did you do? I said: I gave it as charity. He said: You have become liable, unless it was not enough to cover what one could perform hajj with from Makkah. If it did not reach the amount by which hajj could be performed from Makkah, then there is no liability upon you. But if it did reach the amount by which hajj could be performed from Makkah, then you are liable.

key_terms.أَحُجَّ: to perform hajj on behalf of the deceased
key_terms.الْحِجْرِ: the Hijr near the Kaʿbah where the Imam was found
key_terms.الْفُقَهَاءِ: the jurists consulted for legal judgment
key_terms.بِتَرِكَتِهِ: his estate or property left behind after death
key_terms.تَصَدَّقْ: to give the funds as charity
key_terms.ضَمَانٌ: legal liability for failing to carry out the bequest properly
key_terms.ضَمِنْتَ: you have incurred liability or responsibility
key_terms.مِنْ مَكَّةَ: from Makkah, indicating the minimum threshold for hajj expenses

ai.seo_question: If a deceased person bequeathed money for hajj but the amount seems insufficient, may the executor give it in charity instead?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal responsibility of an executor who changes the deceased's bequest from hajj to charity. Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام rules that the executor is liable if the amount was sufficient for performing hajj from Makkah, but not liable if even that minimum could not be met.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5482 - Muhammad bin Abi Umayr narrated from Zayd Al-Narsi, from Ali bin Mazid, the companion of Al-Sabari, who said:

A man entrusted me with his estate and instructed me to perform Hajj on his behalf. When I examined the amount, I found it to be very little and insufficient for Hajj. I asked Abu Hanifa and the jurists of Kufa, and they said: 'Give it in charity on his behalf'.

Later, when I met Abdullah ibn Al-Hasan during Tawaf, I asked him and said:
'A man from your followers in Kufa passed away and entrusted his estate to me, instructing me to perform Hajj on his behalf. However, when I examined the amount, it was not enough for Hajj. I consulted the jurists in my area, and they advised me to give it in charity on his behalf, so I did. What do you say?'
He replied: Here is Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) in the Hijr, go to him and ask him.
So I entered the Hijr, and I saw Abu Abdullah (as) under the Mizab, facing the Kaaba, praying. Then Imam (as) turned, saw me, and asked: What is your need?
I said: A man passed away and entrusted his estate to me to perform Hajj on his behalf, but I found it insufficient for Hajj. I asked the jurists in my area, and they advised me to give it in charity, so I did.
Imam (as) said: What have you done (with the money)?

I replied: I gave it in charity.
Imam (as) said: You are liable - unless the amount was not enough for Hajj even from Mecca. If it was insufficient for Hajj from Mecca, then there is no liability on you. But if it was enough for Hajj from Mecca, then you are responsible.
